title: Race to Twenty-One
problem: Starting from 0, players alternately add an integer from 1 through 4 to a running total. The player who says 21 wins. Can the first player force a win?

hints.text: Try to control the running total modulo 5.
Say 1 first, then make your addition and your opponent's previous addition sum to 5.

solution.setup: The first player aims to control totals 1,6,11,16,21.
solution.reasoning: Start by adding 1. Whenever the opponent adds k in {1,2,3,4}, add 5-k. Each pair of moves adds 5, returning control at the next target total. This guarantees the sequence 1,6,11,16,21 on the first player's turns.
solution.finalAnswer: Yes. Add 1 first, then complement every opponent addition to 5.
solution.sanityCheck: Every legal opponent move has a unique legal complement between 1 and 4.

keyInsight: A modular invariant converts many possible opponent moves into one controlled sequence of target states.
recognitionCues: When legal moves are consecutive integers, look for a constant complementary sum one larger than the maximum move.
commonMistakes: Trying to reach multiples of 5, which gives control to the wrong player for target 21.
followUps: Generalize to moves 1 through m and target N.
